newsitem.title: USA: Nuclear official guilty of leaking information.
newsitem.headline: Nuclear official guilty of leaking information.

text.p: A Nuclear Regulatory Commission official pleaded guilty Friday to illegally disclosing confidential information to a nuclear power plant that is under investigation for allegedly manipulating safety tests in the 1980s.

Edouard Trottier, 53, admitted in U.S. District Court in Portland that he provided officials at Maine Yankee with copies of an NRC investigation that he had been specifically told were not to be distributed outside of the agency.
Federal proseuctor Jay McCloskey said Trottier's actions could "substantially" affect his office's on-going review of that NRC investigation.

The 910-megawatt plant in Wiscasset has been under investigation for more than a year over accusations made by an anonymous whistleblower that plant officials fraudulently manipulated the results of testing on the core cooling system in the 1980s.

The 24-year-old plant has had a series of safety-related shutdowns and investigations in the past three years. The NRC recently placed the plant on a Watch List of troubled plants and is considering fines for 16 alleged safety violations.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro-Electric Co, five percent by Maine Public Service Co, and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
